clue.text: Change hands around

indicators.note: around tells us to turn the word for hands so it runs the other way

parts.note: paws is a jokey word for hands

explanation.surface: Someone moves an object from one hand to the other.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' reverses PAWS.
explanation.definitionFit: To swap is to exchange one thing for another, a kind of change.

clue.text: Actor — will he fancy this kind of work?

indicators.note: fancy as an adjective means elaborate or fanciful, signalling a rearrangement of the letters

explanation.surface: Would an actor like an office job?
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' looks like a verb meaning like, but it rearranges ACTOR and WILL HE.
explanation.definitionFit: White-collar work is office or professional work, a kind of employment.

clue.text: Eat up — tongue's no longer being served

parts.note: a tongue is a language, such as Polish
a dish that is off is no longer available on the menu

explanation.surface: Finishing a meal because the tongue dish has run out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tongue' suggests the meat dish but means a language.
explanation.definitionFit: To polish off food is to eat it all up, an idiom.

clue.text: This can be used to transport the police, right?

definitions.text: This can be used to transport the police, right?

indicators.note: transport can mean to carry away or enrapture, so the letters before it are carried off into a new order

explanation.surface: A question about how the police get flown around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transport' rearranges THE and POLICE into HELICOPTE; R for right completes it, and the whole clue describes the aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: Police forces use rotor aircraft to move officers and observe from the air, so the whole clue describes one.

clue.text: Percy's stolen egg

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, so the clue says Percy is this

parts.note: hot is slang for stolen goods
to egg someone on is to spur them

explanation.surface: Percy has taken an egg that isn't his.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Henry Percy, nicknamed Hotspur, appears in Shakespeare's Henry IV Part 1.
explanation.definitionFit: Harry Percy was nicknamed for his rashness; the nickname is the historical name for him.

clue.text: Play a corking bloke, an anomaly

indicators.note: an anomaly is something irregular, signalling the preceding letters are arranged irregularly

explanation.surface: A corking fellow turns out to be an oddity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'anomaly' rearranges A CORKING BLOKE AN; the grid's IA is a typo for IN.
explanation.definitionFit: John Osborne's 1956 drama about an angry young man is a stage play.

clue.text: Company vote on company doctor, a rather vain fellow

parts.note: X is the mark made on a ballot paper
MB is a medical degree, Bachelor of Medicine

explanation.surface: A firm holds a vote on its in-house physician, who is rather vain.
explanation.definitionFit: A coxcomb is an old word for a conceited dandy, a vain man.

clue.text: Confused by talking

indicators.note: talking means the word is spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: by can mean through, as in by means of

explanation.surface: Someone is muddled by the chatter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'talking' signals that THROUGH, a sense of by, is said aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: If something threw you it disconcerted you, leaving you confused.

clue.text: Strange game

definitions.meaning: old British slang for odd or peculiar
a card game of collecting sets and runs

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both dated slang for odd and the name of a card game.

clue.text: Can produce, verbally or in writing, declaration of love

indicators.note: verbally means spoken, so the phrase given by the words before it is said out loud

parts.note: a billy is a camping can, and do can mean produce or make, giving billy do

explanation.surface: A clue about whether a love declaration can be made in speech or on paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'verbally' signals that BILLY (a billycan) plus DO (produce) is spoken, sounding like the French phrase pronounced 'billy-doo'.
explanation.definitionFit: A billet-doux is a love letter, literally French for a sweet note, so a written declaration of love.

clue.text: Stuff used in macrame

indicators.note: used in says the letters sit inside the word macrame

explanation.surface: Material that goes into knotted macrame work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used in' points to the letters inside maCRAMe.
explanation.definitionFit: To stuff something is to pack it tightly, and to cram means the same.

clue.text: Fluff cat's brought back to me

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: brought back tells us to turn the word for cat around

parts.note: puss is a familiar word for a cat

explanation.surface: Someone's fluffy cat returns to them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fluff' is a verb here, not a cat's fur; the reversed cat follows ME as 'to me' says.
explanation.definitionFit: To fluff a task is to bungle it, which is a synonym of the phrasal verb here.

clue.text: Cotswold village where shows are staged

definitions.meaning: A picturesque village in the Cotswolds, the hill country of south-west England
the New York street famous for its theatres

explanation.definitionFit: The same name belongs to an English village and to the New York theatre district.

clue.text: Drink a quantity? Without you, say, I will; attending a party

indicators.note: Without means the letter for you is taken out of the word before it

parts.note: an amount is a quantity
U stands for you, as in text messages
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A drinker declines company but will go to a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' removes U from A MOUNT to leave AMONT.
explanation.definitionFit: Amontillado is a type of medium sherry, a drink.

clue.text: Game for four or for one

definitions.meaning: a variety of whist, a card game for four players, where one player takes on the other three
something done for one person alone, as a performance by a single performer

explanation.definitionFit: Solo is both the name of a four-handed card game and a word meaning by a single person.

clue.text: Record low music by weaver

parts.note: rock is a style of music
Bottom is the weaver in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream

explanation.surface: Music by a weaver hits an all-time low.
explanation.walkthrough: Bottom, the weaver who is given a donkey's head in A Midsummer Night's Dream, is a classic crossword reference.
explanation.definitionFit: Hitting the lowest possible level is the idiom for a record low.

clue.text: Exultant, thump rail energetically

indicators.note: energetically suggests vigorous movement, signalling the letters are shaken up

explanation.surface: A jubilant person bangs the rail hard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'energetically' rearranges THUMP RAIL.
explanation.definitionFit: Triumphal means celebrating victory, i.e. exultant.

clue.text: Pilot's seeking information on field sport

parts.note: to pilot an aircraft is to fly it
fishing for information means trying to find it out

explanation.surface: An airman asks about a country pursuit.
explanation.definitionFit: Angling with artificial flies is counted among the traditional British field sports.

clue.text: Excess waves link up

parts.note: surf is breaking waves

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a tie is a link or bond

explanation.surface: Too many waves join up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses TIE to EIT in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A surfeit is an excessive amount of something.

clue.text: Man's given girl sandwiches — cheese

definitions.note: a man's given name, i.e. a first name for a man

indicators.note: sandwiches means the girl's name surrounds the cheese

parts.note: gal is an informal word for a girl
Brie is a soft French cheese

explanation.surface: A man hands a girl some cheese sandwiches.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is 'Man's given', short for a man's given name; 'girl' is the informal GAL, not a full name.
explanation.definitionFit: Gabriel is a male first name, borne by the archangel.

clue.text: Enthusiastic about religion,'not keeping quiet

indicators.note: not keeping means the letters for quiet are dropped from the religion

parts.note: Shinto is the traditional religion of Japan
sh is the call for quiet

explanation.surface: Someone is loudly keen on their faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not keeping' removes SH from SHINTO.
explanation.definitionFit: Being into something is the informal idiom for being keen on it.

clue.text: Tests featuring quote about river flowing west, and an inlet

indicators.note: featuring means the word for quote has the river inside it

parts.note: to quote a source is to cite it
R is the abbreviation for river; its direction of flow is only surface colour, as a single letter reads the same either way
a ria is a long narrow coastal inlet

explanation.surface: Exam questions about a westward river and a coastal inlet.
explanation.definitionFit: Criteria are standards by which things are tested or judged.

clue.text: Confusion when Charles falls in love? Just the opposite

indicators.note: falls in suggests one piece dropping inside another
Just the opposite reverses the container roles, so love goes inside Charles

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, written O

explanation.surface: Charles falling in love causes confusion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'falls in' plus 'Just the opposite' means O goes into CHAS, not Charles into love.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaos is utter disorder or confusion.

clue.text: Someone unemployed found one old penny, large, and a sovereign

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
D was the abbreviation for a penny before British decimal coinage
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A jobless person finds a penny and a gold coin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sovereign' suggests the old gold coin but means a monarch, ER.
explanation.definitionFit: An idler is someone doing nothing, without work.

clue.text: Beadle's 11

definitions.meaning: The beadle in Dickens's Oliver Twist, so this is the beadle's name
the answer to 11 across, meaning to botch or bungle

explanation.definitionFit: The beadle in Oliver Twist bears this name, and as a verb it means to botch clumsily.

clue.text: Competent seaman employed by the French

parts.note: AB stands for ...-bodied seaman
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A skilled sailor works for the French.
explanation.definitionFit: Able means having the skill or power to do something, i.e. competent.

clue.text: European team member on American side

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means placed after the other piece

parts.note: in American billiards and pool, english is the term for side, the spin put on a ball
a man is a player in a team

explanation.surface: A European joins an American team as a player.
explanation.walkthrough: British players call cue-ball spin side; Americans call it english.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of England is one kind of European.

clue.text: In the Bible, culprits are mostly converted

indicators.note: converted means changed into another form, so the letters are reshaped
mostly means all but the last letter of the word are is kept

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Most wrongdoers in the Bible end up converted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims ARE to AR; 'converted' rearranges CULPRITS plus AR.
explanation.definitionFit: Scriptural means found in or based on holy writ, so in the Bible.

clue.text: Implement put back into sack

indicators.note: put back tells us to reverse the word for implement

parts.note: a tool is an implement

explanation.surface: A tool is returned to a bag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put back' reverses TOOL.
explanation.definitionFit: To sack a town is to plunder it, which is the verb sense here.
